capabilities: Edit a per-week board of days split into named priority cells
Drag tasks between cells and days
Review the week with a four-step PDCA panel
Show a year overview of ISO week tiles with completion rates
Copy last week's unfinished tasks or move yesterday's into today
disambiguation: Not a task manager with due dates or reminders; it is a weekly board that writes ordinary Markdown checkboxes grouped under cell headings.
extras: Runs fully offline: no network requests, no telemetry, reads and writes only its own files. Requires Obsidian 1.5.7 or later. Ships English and Simplified Chinese; other UI languages fall back to the closest available, and existing files keep the language they were written in. Cells are capped at eight; a day of eight makes the board much taller (551px vs 290px for four in a two-column layout). The daily carry-over only reaches within the current week's file, so Monday needs the weekly move instead. README ends with a link to API documentation that is not included in the text.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to plan a week across days and priority groupings, and task managers that do keep the data outside the vault.
summary: Weekly planning board that splits each day into user-named priority cells and stores tasks as plain Markdown checkboxes, with a year overview and carry-over tools.
